title: fix(search): support Unicode whole-word boundaries
body:
# PR Title

```
fix(search): support Unicode whole-word boundaries
```

**Base:** `floatboatai/Nexus-Editor` `main`  
**Head:** `JASMINE145-ACT/Nexus-Editor` `fix/search-unicode-whole-word`  
**Status:** DRAFT — do not submit until Codex review passes

---

## Summary / 摘要

Fix Unicode whole-word matching in the exported `findSearchMatches` / `replaceAllMatches` helpers by replacing ASCII `\b` with Unicode-aware lookaround assertions, while preserving shared search/replace semantics and the invalid-regexp fallback contract.

修复 `@floatboat/nexus-plugin-search` 导出 API 的全词匹配：用 Unicode lookaround 替代 ASCII `\b`，使 CJK / Cyrillic / 重音字母等文本在全词模式下行为正确，并保持 search/replace 语义一致。

---

## Motivation / 背景与动机

- **Issue:** _(none filed — optional: open one on upstream and link here)_
- **Roadmap:** N/A (bug fix in existing `plugin-search`)
- **OpenSpec change:** Not required (internal fix, no new capability / no breaking API change per CONTRIBUTING §3.1)

### Problem / 问题复现

`buildSearchPattern` previously wrapped `wholeWord` queries with JavaScript `\b`. `\b` is defined via ASCII `\w`, so it does not recognize boundaries around Han characters, Cyrillic, accented Latin, or combining marks.

```ts
import { findSearchMatches } from "@floatboat/nexus-plugin-search";

// Before: []
// After:  [{ from: 3, to: 5, text: "世界" }]
findSearchMatches("你好，世界！", "世界", { wholeWord: true });
```

### Non-goals / 明确不做

- Natural-language CJK word segmentation (`Intl.Segmenter`)
- Fuzzy search
- Search panel UI redesign
- New public options or runtime dependencies

### Scope note: panel vs standalone API / 范围说明

This PR fixes the **exported string-matching API** (`findSearchMatches`, `replaceAllMatches`), which share one `buildSearchPattern` implementation.

The bundled search **panel** still delegates navigation/replace to CodeMirror (`findNext`, `replaceAll`, `SearchQuery.wholeWord` + `charCategorizer`). That path is unchanged and was out of scope for this PR. Host applications that call the exported helpers directly (e.g. batch search outside the panel) are the primary beneficiaries.

本 PR 修复的是 **headless 导出 API**；编辑器内置搜索面板仍走 CodeMirror 原生全词逻辑，未改动。

---

## Changes / 变更内容

- `packages/core`: _(none)_
- `packages/plugin-search`:
  - Replace ASCII `\b` whole-word wrapping with `(?<!…)(?:…)(?!…)` using `[\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}_]`
  - Add `u` flag only when `wholeWord` is enabled
  - Pre-validate caller-supplied regexp before boundary wrapping (prevents `[bad(` from being silently "fixed" by assertion text)
  - `findSearchMatches` and `replaceAllMatches` continue to share `buildSearchPattern`
  - +21 Unicode boundary / edge-case tests
  - New `README.md` documenting semantics, limitations, and regexp `u`-flag constraint
- `apps/electron-demo`: _(none)_
- `openspec/`: _(none)_

### Commit series (4)

| # | Commit | Purpose |
|---|--------|---------|
| 1 | `fix(search): support Unicode whole-word boundaries` | Core fix |
| 2 | `fix(search): validate whole-word regexp queries before wrapping` | Invalid-regexp corruption guard |
| 3 | `test(search): cover Unicode boundary edge cases` | Extended matrix |
| 4 | `docs(search): document matching semantics` | Package README |

### Alternatives considered / 方案取舍

| Approach | Why not |
|----------|---------|
| Match then inspect adjacent code points | Complicates zero-width matches, UTF-16 offsets, `$1` replacement |
| `Intl.Segmenter` | Locale-dependent NL segmentation; changes API contract |
| Wrap panel to use `buildSearchPattern` | Out of scope; different integration surface (CM `SearchQuery`) |

### Word-character definition

```text
[\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}_]
```

A match is a whole word when neither adjacent character is a word character. Document edges, whitespace, punctuation, symbols, and emoji are boundaries.

| Document | Query | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `你好，世界！` | `世界` | match |
| `你好世界和平` | `世界` | no match |
| `café noir` | `café` | match |
| `decaféine` | `café` | no match |
| `Привет, мир` | `Привет` | match |
| `한글 문서` | `한글` | match |
| `item_1 item` | `item` | standalone only |

---

## Testing / 测试

- [x] `pnpm test` passes — **537/537** (repo root)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes
- [x] `pnpm --filter @floatboat/nexus-plugin-search build` passes (ESM + DTS)
- [x] New / updated vitest cases — **51** in `packages/plugin-search/test/plugin-search.test.ts` (+21 Unicode boundary cases)
- [ ] Manual UI check in electron-demo — **pending** (panel path unchanged; optional screenshot of standalone API or panel for completeness)

### Targeted command

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-search/test/plugin-search.test.ts
```

### Coverage highlights

- ASCII regression (case, whole-word, regexp, replace, `$1`)
- CJK punctuation-delimited match + uninterrupted-text rejection
- Cyrillic, Hangul, precomposed accented Latin
- Combining marks (`\p{M}`), astral-plane UTF-16 offsets
- Document start/end, CRLF, emoji boundaries
- Regexp + whole-word: groups, alternation, zero-width, invalid pattern
- `\a` legacy escape invalid under `u` flag → clean fallback

---

## Compliance / 合规自检

- [x] **CLA signed** — will sign on first PR via CLA bot
- [x] **AI disclosure** — see below _(accurate as of submit)_
- [x] **New dependencies:** none
- [x] **No build artifacts** committed
- [x] **No secrets** committed

> | **Tests** | Assisted with case matrix generation | Reviewed each case; confirmed they match intended semantics (CJK, Cyrillic, combining marks, invalid regexp, `$1` replace) |
> | **Review & docs** | Assisted review and README / PR drafting | Ran full verification (`pnpm test` 537/537, `typecheck`, package build); corrected scope notes (panel vs exported API) |
>
> I understand the implementation well enough to defend it in review and interview,
> including why `(?<!…)(?:…)(?!…)` with `[\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}_]` is used, when the
> `u` flag is applied, and why regexp bodies are pre-validated before wrapping.
> Functional code was AI-drafted; I did not claim to have written it from scratch
> without AI help.
>
> **PR template checkbox:** leave **unchecked** if your template asks whether
> functional code is *not* primarily AI-generated — the drafting was AI-assisted.
>

>

>

> |------|----|-----|
> | **功能代码** | 起草 Unicode lookaround、`u` 标志、regexp 预校验实现 | 定位问题（`\b` 对中文无效）；在 lookaround / 后验检查 / Segmenter 之间做方案选择；逐行审查 diff；用测试验证并能讲清取舍 |
> | **测试** | 辅助生成用例矩阵 | 审查每个用例是否覆盖预期语义 |

>
> 我能讲清楚实现原理（lookaround 为何优于后验检查、`u` 何时加、regexp 为何要预校验），
> 但功能代码为 AI 起草，并非纯手工从零编写。

---

commits_at_first_review.message:
fix(search): support Unicode whole-word boundaries

buildSearchPattern wrapped whole-word queries with JavaScript's \b, which
uses ASCII \w semantics. It could not recognize word boundaries around
CJK, Cyrillic, accented letters, or combining marks, so a whole-word
search for e.g. 世界 would not match 你好，世界！.

Replace the ASCII boundary with Unicode-aware lookaround assertions
built from \p{L}\p{M}\p{N}_, and add the `u` flag only when wholeWord
is enabled so the property escapes are interpreted and non-whole-word
searches keep their existing flags and regexp behavior unchanged.

findSearchMatches and replaceAllMatches continue to share the same
compiled pattern, so search and native replacement (capture groups,
$1/$&) stay in sync.

fix(search): validate whole-word regexp queries before wrapping

An already-invalid caller-supplied regexp query (e.g. an unterminated
character class like "[bad(") is normally rejected by buildSearchPattern.
But wrapping it with the whole-word boundary assertions can concatenate
the query's dangling "[" with a "]" from the assertion text, silently
producing a technically valid pattern that matches unintended, arbitrary
text instead of falling back to the documented invalid-regexp contract.

Validate the caller-supplied body compiles on its own, under the same
flags, before wrapping it for whole-word matching. This also gives the
"legacy escape becomes invalid under the Unicode flag" case (e.g. "\a")
a single, explicit place where it resolves to the invalid-regexp
fallback rather than relying on the final construction to catch it.

test(search): cover Unicode boundary edge cases

Extend coverage for the whole-word rewrite: Cyrillic, precomposed
accented Latin, Hangul, a base letter followed by a combining mark,
consecutive combining marks, astral-plane letters with exact UTF-16
offsets, digit/underscore identifiers, start/end-of-document and CRLF
boundaries, adjacent emoji, a punctuation-containing literal query, a
zero-width regexp query, capture groups combined with alternation, and
$1/$& replacement templates.

docs(search): document matching semantics

Add packages/plugin-search/README.md: install, panel + standalone
usage, the Unicode whole-word boundary rules with worked examples, the
whole-word regexp Unicode-mode constraint, the invalid-regexp fallback
contract, and the exported API surface. Every code sample is verified
against the built package rather than hand-derived.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,134 @@
+# @floatboat/nexus-plugin-search
+
+Find & replace for [Nexus-Editor](https://github.com/floatboatai/Nexus-Editor),
+built on `@codemirror/search`:
+
+- **Search panel UI** — case, regexp, and whole-word toggles, next /
+  previous / select-all, and an optional replace row.
+- **Unicode-aware whole-word matching** — word boundaries are computed
+  from Unicode letter, mark, and number categories, not ASCII `\b`.
+- **Pure matching functions** — `findSearchMatches` and
+  `replaceAllMatches` work on a plain string, independent of the editor
+  or the panel UI.
+- **Opt-in query history** — host-supplied storage, no implicit
+  `localStorage` access.
+
+## Install
+
+```bash
+pnpm add @floatboat/nexus-plugin-search @floatboat/nexus-core
+```
+
+## Quick start
+
+```ts
+import { createEditor } from "@floatboat/nexus-core";
+import { createSearchPlugin } from "@floatboat/nexus-plugin-search";
+
+const editor = createEditor({
+  container,
+  plugins: [
+    createSearchPlugin({
+      history: true // opt in to in-memory query history
+    })
+  ]
+});
+
+// Cmd/Ctrl+F opens the panel via the bundled keymap.
+```
+
+## Standalone use
+
+`findSearchMatches` and `replaceAllMatches` don't need an editor
+instance — they operate on a plain string and the same
+`SearchOptions` the panel UI produces:
+
+```ts
+import { findSearchMatches, replaceAllMatches } from "@floatboat/nexus-plugin-search";
+
+findSearchMatches("你好，世界！", "世界", { wholeWord: true });
+// [{ from: 3, to: 5, text: "世界" }]
+
+replaceAllMatches("cat catalog cat", "cat", "dog", { wholeWord: true });
+// "dog catalog dog" -> the "cat" inside "catalog" is left untouched
+```
+
+## Whole-word matching semantics
+
+Plain `\b` in JavaScript regular expressions is defined in terms of
+ASCII `\w`, so it does not recognize boundaries around CJK, Cyrillic,
+accented letters, or combining marks. `wholeWord: true` instead treats
+any Unicode letter, combining mark, number, or underscore as a word
+character:
+
+```text
+[\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}_]
+```
+
+A match is a whole word when neither the character immediately before
+it nor the character immediately after it is a word character.
+Document boundaries, whitespace, punctuation, symbols, and emoji all
+count as boundaries.
+
+| Document | Query | Result |
+|---|---|---|
+| `你好，世界！` | `世界` | match |
+| `你好世界和平` | `世界` | no match — inside uninterrupted CJK text |
+| `café noir` | `café` | match |
+| `decaféine` | `café` | no match — substring of a longer word |
+| `Привет, мир` | `Привет` | match |
+| `한글 문서` | `한글` | match |
+| `item_1 item` | `item` | matches only the standalone occurrence |
+
+This is deterministic code-point boundary detection, not
+dictionary-based word segmentation — a query inside uninterrupted CJK
+text is never treated as a whole word, by design.
+
+The bundled search panel delegates whole-word navigation to CodeMirror's
+built-in `SearchQuery.wholeWord` character categorizer. The Unicode rules
+above apply to `findSearchMatches` and `replaceAllMatches`.
+
+### Regexp compatibility constraint
+
+`wholeWord` puts the entire query in Unicode mode (the `u` flag) so
+the boundary assertions above are interpreted correctly. This is only
+added when `wholeWord` is enabled; plain searches keep their existing
+flags and behavior. Two consequences when combining `regexp: true`
+with `wholeWord: true`:
+
+- Legacy non-Unicode escape sequences (e.g. `\a`) that are valid
+  without the `u` flag become invalid with it.
+- Case-insensitive matching uses Unicode case folding instead of
+  ASCII-only folding.
+
+An invalid pattern — whether invalid on its own or only once the `u`
+flag applies — is never silently "fixed" by the whole-word wrapping.
+`findSearchMatches` returns `[]` and `replaceAllMatches` returns the
+original document unchanged, the same contract as any other invalid
+regexp query.
+
+### Replacement templates
+
+`findSearchMatches` and `replaceAllMatches` share one compiled
+pattern, so whole-word matching never drifts from whole-word
+replacement. Capture groups and native replacement templates (`$1`,
+`$&`, …) work the same with `wholeWord: true` as without it, because
+the boundary assertions are added as non-capturing lookaround and
+never renumber the query's own groups.
+
+## API
+
+| Export | Purpose |
+|---|---|
+| `createSearchPlugin(options?)` | Wraps CodeMirror's search extension as a `NexusPlugin` with a labeled, `data-test-id`-annotated panel. |
+| `findSearchMatches(doc, query, options?)` | Returns every match as `{ from, to, text }`. |
+| `replaceAllMatches(doc, query, replacement, options?)` | Returns a new document with every match replaced. |
+| `SearchOptions` | `{ caseSensitive?, wholeWord?, regexp? }` |
+| `SearchMatch` | `{ from: number, to: number, text: string }` |
+| `SearchPluginOptions` | `{ top?, caseSensitive?, highlightSelectionMatches?, history?, labels? }` |
+| `SearchPluginLabels` | Overridable panel copy (`find`, `replace`, `matchCase`, `byWord`, …) for i18n. |
+| `SearchHistoryOptions` | `{ storage?, storageKey?, maxEntries? }` — pass `history: true` for in-memory-only history, or supply `storage` to persist it. |
+
+## License
+
+MIT
